vulnerabilities.description: Content Security Policy header contains 'unsafe-eval' which violates CSP best practices. This allows inline script execution, defeating CSP protection against XSS attacks. Remove 'unsafe-eval' from production CSP policies.

Token signature validation performed client-side only (HMAC-SHA256). While documented, client-side validation provides only XSS mitigation, not actual security. Server-side validation is required to prevent token forgery. Comment acknowledges this limitation but it remains a security risk.

Fallback to plaintext storage when WebCrypto is unavailable. Modern browsers support WebCrypto, but the fallback `createPlaintextStorage()` silently downgrades to unencrypted storage of sensitive session data, potentially exposing credentials in localStorage.

Cryptographic random ID generation has error-throwing behavior only as last resort. If both crypto.randomUUID() and crypto.getRandomValues() fail, it throws an error, but fallback logic could mask transient crypto failures. Consider explicit fallback policy.
Token format validation regex `/^[a-f0-9-]{36,}$/` is very permissive. Allows any hex + dash combination with 36+ chars. While adequate for UUIDs, consider stricter validation for production use.
Double-init guard checks `window.__IMPECCABLE_LIVE_INIT__` but returns silently without logging. Makes troubleshooting difficult and could mask initialization issues in production.

recommendations: IMMEDIATE: Remove 'unsafe-eval' from CSP headers in src/server.test.ts and ensure production CSP is strict. CSP should use 'strict-dynamic' with nonces instead.
Implement server-side token signature validation as a hard requirement. Do not rely on client-side validation alone.
Replace plaintext storage fallback with explicit error handling. Force HTTPS + WebCrypto or gracefully degrade with user notification instead of silent downgrade.
Add structured logging for cryptographic failures and init guard hits to improve observability and debugging.
Implement stricter token format validation; consider UUID v4 validation or a custom format whitelist.
Review and audit the Supabase auth middleware (src/integrations/supabase/auth-middleware.ts) for proper JWT validation, expiration handling, and CORS configuration.
Scan dependencies for known vulnerabilities: Run `npm audit` or `bun audit` and address any high/critical findings.
Ensure all API routes (src/routes/api/*) use proper authentication middleware and validate all user inputs.
Add HTTP Strict-Transport-Security (HSTS) and X-Content-Type-Options headers to server responses.
Review encryption key derivation in live-browser-crypto.js; consider using a server-provided salt instead of user-derived salt for better security.
Enable database RLS (Row-Level Security) for all tables and audit permission grants regularly.
Implement rate limiting on authentication endpoints to prevent brute-force attacks.
